newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SEC clears Surgutneftegaz for ADRs.
newsitem.headline: SEC clears Surgutneftegaz for ADRs.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has given OAO Surgutneftegaz, one of Russia's biggest oil companies, permission to proceed with an application to issue American Depositary Receipts, the company's parent Surgut Holding said on Wednesday.
A statement from Surgut Holding (NK Surgutneftegaz) said the SEC had granted Surgutneftegaz an exemption from the requirement to disclose information to U.S. standards under its rule 12g32b.
The SEC requires foreign companies intending to issue level-one ADRs to have this exemption.
Surgutneftegaz management announced in May it intended to issue ADRs by the end of this year.
ADRs, issued by U.S. banks and representing shares issued by a foreign company, allow U.S. investors to trade foreign shares while avoiding foreign settlement and custody problems.
Level-one ADRs give investors access to a company's shares, but do not raise new capital.
